bug_semantics: In the Microsoft Teams message handler, groupPolicy="allowlist" was meant to enforce both route admission and sender admission. When a configured channels.msteams.teams team/channel route matched but effectiveGroupAllowFrom was empty, the handler treated the route match as sufficient: the original condition skipped the empty-sender-allowlist rejection, and a later semantics-preserving refactor made that bypass explicit by passing ["*"] to evaluateSenderGroupAccessForPolicy. Consequently any sender in a matched Teams route could reach conversationStore/dispatch and trigger a reply despite not being sender-allowlisted.
flaw_origin: c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f ('feat(channels): add resolve command + defaults', 2026-01-18) is the smallest Git BIC. It introduced route gating into extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts and changed the empty effectiveGroupAllowFrom guard from unconditional rejection to rejection only when !channelGate.allowlistConfigured; it then performed a sender match only when effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length > 0. Its direct parent b54333937335674d7d3d4de8d35810c146d7ec26 had no pre-authorization route gate and unconditionally returned when the effective group sender allowlist was empty. Commit 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6 later preserved, rather than introduced, the behavior by synthesizing ["*"].

No later-commit or fix-commit signal was used.

Refactor rejection: blame at fix^ assigns the explicit wildcard lines to 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6, while its parent already has c7ea's equivalent bypass. Fix: `git show 88aee9161e0e6d32e810a25711e32a808a1777b2` removes the ternary/wildcard and always passes effectiveGroupAllowFrom, adding the empty-list regression test. Release source at v2026.3.7 contains the wildcard ternary; v2026.3.8 contains `groupAllowFrom: effectiveGroupAllowFrom`. Ancestry checks show c7ea is absent from v2026.1.16-2 and present in the next repository tag v2026.1.20, while 88aee916 is absent from v2026.3.7 and present in v2026.3.8. GitHub's commit-to-pulls API returns [] for c7ea, and the commit is a one-parent direct commit, so there is no reconstructable squash member set. Marker: the BIC commit object has no AI attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerable authorization decision first becomes possible in c7ea: a matched route makes an empty sender allowlist pass, whereas the direct parent rejects every empty sender allowlist. The March refactor only re-expresses that same decision as a wildcard and therefore is not the BIC. The direct fix 88aee916 restores conjunction of route and sender authorization and is carried by the first patched stable tag v2026.3.8. Because the audit protocol permits AI attribution only from the BIC commit object and that object contains a human identity with no qualifying AI marker or bot identity, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
